A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STAMP. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–L are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original contamination-detection experiments, ablations, false-positive analyses, and automated and human evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, case studies, and evaluations, including the 40-author study and appendix comparisons.

M1.justification: Watermarked public/private rephrasing, perplexity comparison, outlier clipping, the one-sided paired t-test, and averaging over private keys remain unchanged. Removing a redundant random-key footnote does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same four benchmarks, OpenWebText, EMNLP 2024 abstracts, AI Snake Oil articles, and contamination scenarios. v2's erroneous EMNLP 2001 citation does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: The same comparisons retain PaCoST, both LLM DI variants, five membership-inference attacks, Unicode watermarking, and Appendix H's radioactivity method. Citation-year and suffix updates do not introduce different comparators.

E3.justification: Training budgets, benchmark sampling, duplication rates, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and human-study sample sizes match. Appendix H also retains its distinct four-repeat comparison protocol.

E4.justification: Watermarking and paired-test ablations, sample-size/key-count/corpus-size analyses, partial contamination, false-positive tests, and case studies are retained. The new author-rating chart visualizes an existing evaluation.

E5.justification: Statistical testing and reporting remain unchanged, including ten seeded runs for the benchmark-size analysis, five-fold classifier cross-validation, and semantic-score averaging across nine watermark keys.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–12 and the existing plots match. New Figure 4 redisplays the previously reported author ratings: 4 preferred, 24 acceptable, 11 requiring minor edits, and 1 requiring major edits.

T1.justification: The membership hypotheses, watermark formalism, and Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The claims of reliable membership detection under minimal contamination, preserved content utility, and applicability to abstracts and blogs remain. The shortened abstract wording does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations are retained. Both identify the same limitations: watermarking before publication, token-probability access, possible rephrasing errors, and evaluation through continual rather than from-scratch pretraining.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code and model availability; v2 states that code, data, and models are available at the same repository. Training details, watermark parameters, and prompt templates otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the EMNLP 2024 proceedings reference with EMNLP 2001 proceedings, inconsistently with the retained case-study description. Other changes largely update publication metadata for the same works; research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract and sentence edits, removes a redundant footnote, updates acknowledgments and conference information, and revises bibliographic metadata. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the author-rating bar chart as Figure 4, renumbers the existing partial-contamination plot as Figure 5, adds a title icon, and makes small table-label and layout changes. Existing scientific displays otherwise retain their content.

improvement.justification: The reported code, data, and model availability improves reproducibility information, and Figure 4 makes the existing human evaluation easier to assess. These modest gains are partly offset by the erroneous EMNLP 2001 citation in Section 5 and Appendix I. The underlying scientific evidence is unchanged.
